How Much Is a New Mansory-Tuned Audi RS Q8?
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Audi’s Q8 blew eight candles off its birthday cake earlier this year, and that makes it old in today’s automotive game. This is why some might think that production of this model ended, but that’s not the case, because it is still being put together at the Bratislava factory in Slovakia.
By the way, it’s not the only model based on the Volkswagen Group’s old MLB Evo platform to still be around, as this also applies to the Lamborghini Urus, third-gen Porsche Cayenne, and Bentley Bentayga, and the latter is even older, as assembly commenced back in 2015. The previous Audi Q7, Q8, and A6, the demised VW Touareg, and other vehicles also utilized this construction.
Everyone and their pet knows that the Audi Q8 takes on the likes of the BMW X6 and Mercedes GLE Coupe, whereas its range-topping version, the RS Q8, is a rival to the likes of the X6 M and GLE 63 Coupe. The RS Q8 was unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show back in 2019, sharing its V8 lump with the era’s RS 6 and RS 7. Like the lesser SQ8 , it has a ZF eight-speed automatic transmission, and quattro all-wheel drive.
We will delve a bit more into the oily bits in just a few moments, but first, let’s put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery, which has been tuned by Mansory, and is now looking for a new home in the United States of America. This Audi RS Q8 is a 2026 model year car, and it has only 644 miles (1,036 km) under its belt. Therefore, you are looking at a brand-new machine, and it can be yours, if you have deep pockets and want it.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Care to talk about the novelties? Well, these include stuff such as the add-ons in the front bumper, including the new apron with blades on the sides, the extra daytime running lights below the side vents, and the vented hood, among other things. The wheel arches are now on the muscular side of things, so this Audi RS Q8 is now wider than the stock one. There are also new side skirt attachments on deck, as we can see from these pictures.
The images also reveal the back end of this premium mid-size super crossover coupe, which features an entirely new diffuser. The latter element has a five-slat diffuser that is very aggressive. The tailpipes are no longer the OEM ones, as the dual oval exhaust tips have been replaced by new ones. The vehicle has a matte black look on the outside, some glossy black elements, some dry carbon accents, and even forged carbon elements.
The wheels are also new, and they are not oversized. They spin around the red brake calipers, and these are the things that provide the most contrast on the outside. Step inside and you will see bright orange leather upholstery on the seats, on the lower parts of the dashboard, and on the central section of the steering wheel. The cockpit also features some Alcantara elements, as well as red stitching, and some carbon fiber trim, among other things.
Elsewhere, this modded Audi RS Q8 has a digital gauge cluster, an infotainment system in the middle of the dashboard, and a third display to control the HVAC system. There is also a large panoramic sunroof, and the images shared in the gallery reveal other things that one would expect from such a thing.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Weirdly, the vendor, which is known as @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, hasn’t mentioned the oily bits at all. And while that would normally mean that the powertrain hasn’t been modded, this is Mansory that we are talking about, so we are not entirely certain that the assembly retains its stock output and thrust.
If it is stock, then you are looking at 631 bhp (640 ps/571 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque. A bone stock Audi RS Q8 takes just 3.4 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and that makes it roughly two-tenths of a second slower than the new Lamborghini Urus SE Performante, which has 801 hp (812 ps/598 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque combined from its plug-in hybrid V8.
Now, we have told you everything that we know about the pictured Audi RS Q8 with Mansory goodies save for the asking price. So, how much do you think you have to pay if you want to buy it? That would be $269,995. By comparison, a brand-new Audi RS Q8 performance from the 2027 model year will set you back a minimum of $139,700, which is the official MSRP in the United States of America.
Is this tuned example worth more than $100K more? You be the judge of that, and feel free to tell us what you think about it in the comments area below. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)
